```text
# PR #3250: Patch: draw the dungeon map's node icons as SVG instead of system emoji

Closes #3229

## What changed

The dungeon map's ten node kinds used system emoji. Each kind is now an inline SVG icon: single colour in `currentColor`, on a 24-unit grid, with rounded 1.8 strokes.

- **`dungeon/map/NodeIcon.tsx`** (new): `NodeIcon({ kind })` draws one glyph per `RunNodeKind`. The glyphs sit in an exhaustive `Record<RunNodeKind, ReactElement>`, so a new kind in the Rust enum breaks the build rather than the screen. The SVG is `aria-hidden` and holds no `<text>`, no `<title>` and no colour literal.
- **`dungeon/map/MapScreen.tsx`**: `NODE_META` is now `NODE_LABELS`, labels only, and the icon span renders `<NodeIcon>`. `aria-label`, `title`, every `data-*`, the testids and `onClick` are unchanged. The file holds no emoji, comments included.
- **`dungeon/map/run.css`**: the icon is a 24 px `inline-flex` box coloured from `--node-color`. Ten `.dungeon-run-map__node[data-kind=…]` rules set it from existing `--pal-*` tokens (fight red-400, elite orange-400, ghost slate-100, miniBoss ember-500, boss gold-300, shop green-400, campfire yellow-400, event purple-400, chest brass-500, shrine cyan-400). There is no new colour literal and `palette.css` is untouched.
- **Tests**:
  - `RunScreen.test.tsx`: the B27 tests now assert `svg[data-icon=<kind>]` instead of the emoji text.
  - `NodeIcon.test.tsx` (new): each kind draws a distinct `currentColor` SVG on the 24 grid, with no text, title or colour literal. The map renders all ten kinds, each button has its accessible name ("Fight 1", "Final boss 2" and so on), `data-kind` and testid, exactly one SVG inside `.dungeon-run-map__icon[aria-hidden]`, and ASCII-only text.
  - `noEmoji.test.ts` (new): scans every `.ts`, `.tsx` and `.css` file under `apps/web/src/dungeon/` for emoji code points. A second test checks that the scan flags emoji, VS16 and flags but passes plain text and an arrow. The pattern uses escapes only.
- **`apps/web/README.md`**: one paragraph saying where the node icons live and that `dungeon/` holds no emoji.

## Testing (commands I ran)

- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/dungeon`: 11 files, 90 tests passed. This run first built the wasm module.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/dungeon src/palette.test.ts src/writing.test.ts`: 13 files, 100 tests passed.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`: clean.
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/dungeon`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`: OK.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: `1767 rulings, 4337 proofs, 53459 citations in 3438 files, 23121 links: ok`. The change cites no R-id.
- I checked that the scan catches an emoji. With ⚔️ temporarily in `MapScreen.tsx` it failed with `map/MapScreen.tsx:4`. I restored the file and it passes.

I did not run the e2e suite. No dungeon e2e spec exists (`grep` finds none under `e2e/`), so CI's `e2e smoke` job is the only e2e coverage. No Rust file changed, so I did not run clippy or `cargo test`.

## Decisions the issue left open

- **Hand-written inline TSX glyphs, as in `SettingsButton.tsx`.** I rejected a Python generator like `scripts/brand-logo.py`, so no generator script is committed.
- **Colour by node kind only.** I rejected colouring by state as well, because the map already shows reachable, current and disabled through border, shadow and opacity.
- **Motifs:**
  - Mini-boss is a horned skull; I rejected a dragon as too detailed at 24 px.
  - Chest is a treasure chest; I rejected a gift box.
  - Stroke width is 1.8, between the client's existing 1.6 and 2.2.

## Departures from the plan

- The emoji pattern uses alternation (`…|\u{FE0F}|\u{200D}|\u{20E3}`) instead of the planned character class `[\u{FE0F}\u{200D}\u{20E3}]`. ESLint's `no-misleading-character-class` rejects the class, and I would not add a disable. The two forms match the same code points.
```
